He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University Blue Devils]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/SportSelect.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&SPID=1845&SPSID=22727&KEY=&Q_SEASON=2015|title=Men's Basketball – Roster – Duke University Blue Devils|work=GoDuke.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}} He was one of the top-rated basketball recruits in the class of 2011, a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]],{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2011/02/2011-McDonalds-Team.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721062025/http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2011/02/2011-McDonalds-Team.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 21, 2011|title=2011 McDonald's All-American Game boys' rosters announced|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}} and is the younger brother and former high school and college teammate of both [[Mason Plumlee|Mason]] and [[Miles Plumlee]]. ==High school career== A native of [[Warsaw, Indiana]], Plumlee joined his older brothers as boarding students at [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] in [[Arden, North Carolina]]. During his four years on the basketball team, the Greenies won 139 out of 150 games, winning four consecutive state championships. Plumlee's contribution to the team increased each year. By his junior year, when both his brothers were playing for Duke, Plumlee averaged 8.6 points, 8.0 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks per game. As a senior, Plumlee averaged 11.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks per game. Following that season, the {{convert|6|ft|11|in|adj=on|m}} Plumlee was named the [[Gatorade]] Player of the Year in North Carolina and named to the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2011 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/hZlBoe-lrUWxbBGYXAO0Xw/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-marshall-plumlee.htm|title=Marshall Plumlee (Christ School High School) Basketball Stats|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/OaY5WYJMu0qADRDbOPMT0A/christ-school-greenies/basketball-winter-07-08/schedule.htm|title=Christ School 2007-08 Basketball Schedule|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/OaY5WYJMu0qADRDbOPMT0A/christ-school-greenies/basketball-winter-08-09/schedule.htm|title=Christ School 2008-09 Basketball Schedule|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/OaY5WYJMu0qADRDbOPMT0A/christ-school-greenies/basketball-winter-09-10/schedule.htm|title=Christ School 2009-10 Basketball Schedule|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/iX66gwrULESGqr0e3lNpIg/basketball-winter-10-11/stats-marshall-plumlee.htm|title=Marshall Plumlee (Christ School High School) Basketball Stats|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}} As a senior, Plumlee signed to play for [[Duke men's basketball|Duke University]].{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Watson|url=http://bluedevilnation.net/2010/07/marshall-plumlee-to-duke/|title=Breaking News – Marshall Plumlee to Duke|work=BlueDevilNation.net|date=July 10, 2010|access-date=April 6, 2013}} Plumlee's five-player recruiting class for [[Duke men's basketball|Duke]] in 2011 included [[Austin Rivers]], [[Alex Murphy (basketball)|Alex Murphy]], [[Quinn Cook]], and [[Michael Gbinije]]. Duke's class was the second-best recruiting class in 2011, according to [[ESPNU]].{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/classrankings?classyear=2011&classmonth=4&rank=2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220225181526/http://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/classrankings?classyear=2011&classmonth=4&rank=2|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 25, 2022|title=2013 Basketball Class Rankings|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 30, 2023}} ==College career== In Plumlee's freshman year at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], both of his brothers were on the team and Marshall redshirted.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=205214164&Q_SEASON=2011|title=Marshall Plumlee Bio|work=GoDuke.com|access-date=April 6, 2013}} He made his debut in 2012–13, but his playing time was limited by a stress fracture in his foot. In Plumlee's junior year (2014–15), he saw limited action, playing 8.5 minutes per game in 30 contests. By his junior year, Plumlee had developed into a steady inside defender, backing up [[Jahlil Okafor]], a freshman who went on to be the 3rd pick in [[2015 NBA draft|that year's NBA draft]]. That 2015 Duke team won the NCAA national championship. During his final season at Duke, Plumlee served as a team captain along with [[Amile Jefferson]] and [[Matt Jones (basketball)|Matt Jones]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Hoerger|url=http://www.dukechronicle.com/blog/blue-zone/2015/04/jefferson-plumlee-matt-jones-named-duke-basketball-captains-2015-16|title=Jefferson, Plumlee, Matt Jones named Duke basketball captains for 2015-16|work=DukeChronicle.com|date=April 24, 2015|access-date=October 26, 2015}} Plumlee started all 36 games that year, averaging 8.3 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 1.6 blocked (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Plumlee joined the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Knicks to Participate in Orlando Pro Summer League|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-participate-orlando-pro-summer-league|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2016|access-date=June 28, 2016}} On July 8, 2016, he signed with the Knicks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-marshall-plumlee|title=Knicks Sign Marshall Plumlee|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments to the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 8, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}} Plumlee made his NBA debut on November 20, 2016, against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was rushed into the city from his D-League assignment when starting center [[Joakim Noah]] was sent home due to illness. He gathered a rebound and committed a foul in five minutes of action in a win over the Hawks.{{cite web |date=November 20, 2016 |title=Anthony has 31, Knicks beat Hawks for 4th straight home win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899643 |access-date=November 20, 2016 |work=ESPN.com}} On July 7, 2017, he was waived by the Knicks.{{cite web|author=NY_KnicksPR|url=https://twitter.com/NY_KnicksPR/status/883321663051489280|title=July 7, 2017 – The New York Knickerbockers...|work=Twitter|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}} ===Agua Caliente Clippers (2017–2018)=== On September 27, 2017, Plumlee signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-training-camp-roster-2017|title=Press Release: L.A. CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2017}} He was waived by the Clippers on October 14, 2017, after appearing in four preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-announcement-171014/|title=Press Release: L.A. CLIPPERS CONVERT C.J. WILLIAMS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT, WAIVE IROEGBU, PLUMLEE & WALLACE|work=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017}} A week later, he was named in the inaugural [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=http://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-of-ontario-announce-2017-18-camp-roster/|title=Agua Caliente Clippers of Ontario Announce 2017-18 Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017|archive-date=November 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117123448/http://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-of-ontario-announce-2017-18-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} He went on to earn a spot in the team's opening-night roster.{{cite web|url=http://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-of-ontario-announce-2017-18-opening-night-roster/|title=Agua Caliente Clippers of Ontario Announce 2017-18 Opening Night Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017|archive-date=November 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117123336/http://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/news/agua-caliente-clippers-of-ontario-announce-2017-18-opening-night-roster/|url-status=dead}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2018)=== On January 15, 2018, Plumlee signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Throughout the season, he split his playing time between the Bucks and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Wisconsin Herd]]. ==National team career== Plumlee played with the senior [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]], where the team won the gold medal. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2016}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 New York Knicks season|New York]] | '''21''' || '''1''' || '''8.1''' || '''.533''' || – || .421 || '''2.4''' || '''.5''' || '''.2''' || '''.2''' || '''1.9''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{Nbay|2017}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 8 || 0 || 6.5 || .333 || – || '''.750''' || 2.1 || .3 || .0 || .1 || 1.8 |- |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan=2| Career | 29 || 1 || 7.7 || .515 || – || .571 || 2.3 || .4 || .1 || .2 || 1.9 {{S-end}} ==Military career== Plumlee earned a commission into the [[United States Army]] as an infantry officer through Duke University's [[Reserve Officers' Training Corps]] (ROTC) program. He participated in a ROTC contracting ceremony on January 23, 2015, on the court of [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=205214164|title = Marshall Plumlee - 2015-16 - Men's Basketball}} Upon graduating from Duke, Plumlee commissioned into the [[New York National Guard]] in 2017, while playing for the New York Knicks. In 2019, Plumlee graduated from [[Ranger School]], with his mother affixing the Ranger Tab, and transitioned to an active-duty military status. According to Plumlee, his inspiration to serve in the military stemmed from his childhood just as his desire to play professional basketball. General [[Robert Brooks Brown]], a retired commanding general of [[United States Army Pacific]], became a mentor of Plumlee's in high school. Both men played collegiate basketball under coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]].{{cite web | last=Garland | first=Chad | title=Ranger School graduates include first woman in Air Force to earn tab, 7-foot former NBA player | website=Stars and Stripes | date=2019-09-02 | url=https://www.stripes.com/news/ranger-school-graduates-include-first-woman-in-air-force-to-earn-tab-7-foot-former-nba-player-1.596961 | access-date=2025-12-13}} ==Business career== In May 2022, Plumlee announced that he would be entering the two-year [[MBA]] program at [[Harvard Business School]], joining the HBS class of 2024.{{cite web | url=https://thespun.com/more/top-stories/look-former-duke-star-attending-harvard-business-school | title=Look: Former Duke Star Attending Harvard Business School }} ==Personal life== Plumlee grew up with brothers [[Miles Plumlee|Miles]] and [[Mason Plumlee|Mason]], and they reunited during the 2011–12 basketball season at Duke University; they also have a sister named Madeleine, who played volleyball at the [[University of Notre Dame]].{{cite web |title=Maddie Plumlee |url=https://und.com/roster/maddie-plumlee/ |website=Notre Dame Athletics The Fighting Irish |date=July 10, 2018 |access-date=December 18, 2021}} They were only the third trio of brothers to play on the same college basketball team at the same time. His parents are Millard "Perky" (a former [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech basketball]] player) and Leslie Plumlee (a former [[Purdue University|Purdue]] [[Purdue Boilermakers women's basketball|women's basketball]] player who set the school single-game rebound record with 25).{{cite
